name: declarative-charts
description: Create beautiful charts using declarative HTML elements. Bar, line, pie, funnel charts with accessibility, palettes, and responsive design.
//engines: Vite 8 requires ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0 and is the binding constraint; vitest needs ^20 || ^22 || >=24 and happy-dom >=20. Consumers need far less - the artifacts are ES2020 with no Node APIs - but Node 18 reached end of life in April 2025, so there is nothing below this worth promising support for.
//sideEffects: Defining custom elements IS the side effect. Marking this package side-effect-free lets bundlers drop `import 'declarative-charts'` entirely, registering nothing and rendering a blank page with no error. `*.ts` matters even though no TypeScript is published: Rollup consults this field when building the example gallery from src/, and without it the whole library was tree-shaken out of the site.

scripts.build: tsc && vite build && vite build --config vite.config.standalone.ts && node build/minify-standalone.mjs && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json && npm run analyze
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run test:run && npm run build && npm run test:package && npm run test:visual

author: Lawrence Lustig <larrylustig@gmail.com>
